added.title: Senior Environmental Assessment and Approvals Specialist
added.description:
Senior Environmental Assessment and Approvals Specialist – Permanent and 12 month Secondment / Max Term Contract – Perth CBD

We have two upcoming opportunities for Senior Assessment & Approvals Specialists to join our team on a Permanent and 12-month secondment / maximum term contract.

In this role, you will lead and support the development of strategic network plans and asset strategies. Your primary focus will be on clearly identifying SHE requirements associated with our work programs, influencing external stakeholders to secure strategic safety and environment statutory approvals and requirements for future growth, development and protection of the network.

Your Role in Action

Identify key environmental, planning and/or heritage constraints to facilitate project design, scoping and successful delivery and assist Western Power in delivering outcomes by providing timely and relevant environmental advice (including technical/operational, approvals, strategy and risk).
Supporting and mentoring the business to identify, assess, manage and acquit SHE requirements, including but not limited to environmental, pollution, land access, urban and regional planning and public safety requirements during the planning, development and prioritisation of the work program and associated projects in a timely manner.
Influence the development of strategic network plans, asset strategies, network design standards and work programs that lead to improved SHE outcomes and reduction of associated risk to a level that is as low as reasonably practicable.
Lead and support the development and implementation of SHE requirements that govern access to the network for the purpose of construction, maintenance and inspection and promote improved SHE outcomes.
Develop and manage relationships with external planning and infrastructure stakeholders to ensure the appropriate placement of our network assets, in consideration of our objectives.
Monitor and implement improvements to SHE requirements to ensure continuous improvement of as part of a closed loop feedback process.
Provide Subject Matter Expertise and advice in relation to environment, heritage and urban and regional planning advice to the SHE or SP&A Function and broader business.
Representing the SHE or SP&A Function at internal and external engagement and training sessions.

What Makes You a Great Fit

Bachelor’s Degree in environmental science, science, urban and regional planning, law or related discipline
Solid experience in environment, heritage and statutory planning approvals.
Experience in Public and environmental safety matters and the development of risk reducing performance improvement strategies
Excellent stakeholder management, communication and written skills
Proven ability to influence key internal and external stakeholders in relation to SEQT outcomes
Demonstrated experience with community engagement
Demonstrated ability to work within a dynamic environment and to work autonomously
A sound understanding of the regulations and arrangements associated with infrastructure planning, land development, environmental assessments, and heritage and land access.
Experience managing environmental consultants is desirable, including consultant engagement, contract performance and financial management

By joining Western Power, you will contribute to powering a cleaner energy future. We are dedicated to fostering career development and promoting a healthy work-life balance, empowering you to drive innovation as we develop a network that will serve the Western Australian community for generations. You will also benefit from a range of perks and opportunities, including:

Over 50% of our employment opportunities are driven by career progression.
Flexible work arrangements to support part time work, working hours, working from home arrangements and job share.
The opportunity to purchase up to four weeks of additional leave per year.
Access to salary packaging, social club activities, and discounted health insurance and gym membership.
An award-winning employee recognition and benefits programme.
An innovative team culture that’s enabling the transition to renewable energy and decarbonisation.
In addition to standard leave, enjoy three wellness leave days each year.
Access to end-of-trip facilities at our Perth office and South Metro Depot, perfect for cyclists.
On-site café available for convenient meals and refreshments throughout the day.
22 weeks paid parental leave and 5 days of First Nations cultural leave to support family and cultural connections.

Applications close on 6 November 2026.

We value diversity and inclusivity, encouraging applications from all backgrounds, including women, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, and LGBTQIA+ communities. As a WORK180-endorsed employer for women, we are proud of our commitment to inclusion. You can learn more about this through our Reconciliation Action Plan and Disability Access and Inclusion Plan.

Learn more about Western Power here: About (westernpower.com.au)
Find out how we’re building A Network for Life: A network for life (westernpower.com.au)

added.title: Environmental Specialist - Shoreline/Aquatic Invasive Species
added.description:
The hiring range for this position is $74,430 - $83,242. The full range for this position is $74,430 - $104,118. This is an onsite roll in Willmar, MN.

The Environmental Specialist is responsible for the administration and enforcement of environmental programs related to shoreline management and aquatic invasive species (AIS) within Kandiyohi County. This position involves overseeing shoreline alteration permitting and AIS prevention efforts. The role requires coordination with various local, state, and federal agencies, as well as watercraft users and the public.

Job Duties:
Oversee shoreline alteration permitting according to the Kandiyohi County Shoreland Ordinance, including grading, filling, vegetative alterations, retaining walls, decks, boat houses, and other structures within shoreland areas.
Conduct field inspections to ensure compliance with shoreline management regulations and document findings. Coordinate with Kandiyohi Soil and Water Conservation District and MN DNR Conservation Officers on enforcement actions and implementing restoration orders when violations are identified. 
Provide public education and guidance regarding shoreline best management practices.
Assist in the implementation and administration of the Kandiyohi County Zoning Ordinance.
Help prepare for and attend planning and zoning public hearings.
Assist with the permitting, installation, and inspection of subsurface sewage treatment systems (SSTS) within the county.
Develop and deliver training and educational materials for AIS prevention and proper inspection procedures.
Supervise and support seasonal AIS watercraft inspectors and decontamination specialists.
Use scheduling tools, such as WhenIWork, to manage AIS staff schedules based on public water access site usage and staff availability.
Monitor, inspect, and decontaminate equipment as required, including watercraft, trailers, and docks.
Lead watercraft inspections and decontaminations at designated lakes, including surveying and community outreach.
Perform regular staff support checks, maintain professional communication, and enforce adherence to AIS procedures.
Serve as AIS Coordinator to address emerging challenges and improve work conditions.
Maintain accurate records of inspections, decontaminations, and compliance checks.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:
Associate degree or Bachelor’s Degree in Environmental Studies, Biology, Natural Resource Management, or a related field preferred. Equivalent combinations of relevant certifications, education, and/or experience will be considered.
Minimum of two years of experience in environmental management or related areas.
Supervisory experience in program management or environmental services preferred.

Supplemental Information:
Knowledge:
Shoreland alteration permitting and AIS management.
Relevant environmental laws and regulations at the local, state, and federal levels.
Techniques for shoreline inspection, permitting, and enforcement.
Watercraft inspection and decontamination procedures.
Best practices in program management, training, and public outreach.
Basic computer applications, including Excel, Microsoft Office, GIS, and scheduling software.

Skills:

Performing field inspections and evaluations of shoreland areas and watercraft.
Conducting staff training and public information sessions.
Preparing and maintaining accurate reports and records.
Using computer software for data management and scheduling.
Communicating effectively with stakeholders, including the public, agency personnel, and watercraft users.

Certifications:

Ability to obtain relevant environmental management certifications as required.
Ability to obtain Minnesota Pollution Control Agency SSTS Certification.

Physical Requirements:

Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds.
Ability to walk, stand, bend, and kneel for extended periods during field inspections.
Capable of working outdoors in various weather conditions.
Must be able to perform the essential physical duties of the job with or without reasonable accommodation.

Additional Information:

Must possess a valid Minnesota Driver’s License and maintain a clean driving record.
Must pass a background check.
Must be a U.S. citizen or legally authorized to work in the United States.

Kandiyohi County is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

added.title: Hazardous Waste Field Chemist
added.description:
The CleanPack Chemist
is responsible for

identifying, classifying, and processing hazardous and non-hazardous materials
for collection, packing, and disposal.

Their duties include

performing on-site chemical assessments
segregating wastes according to regulatory and compatibility guidelines
preparing detailed labels and manifests

They collaborate with field teams to ensure compliance with EPA, DOT, and OSHA standards
, maintaining a safety-first culture.

This role supports environmental protection efforts
and provides opportunities to develop skills in

analytical, regulatory, and industrial chemistry
.

Candidates should possess relevant chemistry knowledge and a strong commitment to safety and compliance.
